49660.summary: The class explores God's master plan for the earth, focusing on the theme of God's glory and the fulfillment of promises to Abraham and David. It covers the character of God, the purpose of the universe, and the significance of the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ in fulfilling God's plan.

49661.summary: The class focuses on God's character as expressed in Exodus 34:5-7, emphasizing God's mercy, grace, long-suffering, and forgiveness. It contrasts these attributes with the need for justice and explores how God's character influences His actions towards humanity.

49662.summary: Biblical names reveal God's character and purpose; God's name Yahweh means "I will be," proclaiming his intention to fill the earth with his glory and character. Understanding God's memorial name opens the meaning of scripture and helps believers grasp the unified plan spanning Genesis to Revelation.

49663.summary: The class explores the significance of God being referred to as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, focusing on the promises given to these three generations and their representation of God as a father, a son, and a multitude. It examines the promises and their implications for both Jews and Gentiles.

49664.summary: The class explores the manifestation of God's name, Yahweh, in both the Old and New Testaments, emphasizing that God has always been known as Father and that the name Yahweh does not disappear in the New Testament. It also delves into Jesus' role in manifesting God's name and character, culminating in his crucifixion and resurrection.
